The Riemann sums for 3x^2 on [1,4] are said to approach about 8.1-8.3, yet they are then said to approach 63 from below. Left sums with 20/40/80 rectangles are about 59.7, 61.3, 62.2 (recomputed).

The survey's margin of error is given as plus or minus 4 points for a sample of 90 and never corrected. For n=90 the 95% margin is about plus or minus 10 points (1.96*sqrt(0.25/90)).
The crossword clue is given as seven letters and answered with 'circumlocution', which has 14 letters.

The narrator says no servant speaks a word in Jane Eyre chapter 4. Bessie has several lines of dialogue with Jane in that chapter (Gutenberg text gutenberg.org/files/1260, fetched).

The packet is called a real Supreme Court case about a girl suspended for an anti-money banner, and no such case exists. The real banner case, Morse v. Frederick, involved a male student, 'BONG HiTS 4 JESUS', and a ruling for the school (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morse_v._Frederick, fetched).
Union dues deducted whether or not the worker joins matches Canada's Rand formula (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rand_formula, fetched).
The narrator says reverse image search as a method has existed only since Google's 2011 feature. TinEye launched reverse image search in 2008 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TinEye, fetched).

A G clef curled around the first line is said to make the written notes sound a third lower. A G clef on line 1 (French violin clef) makes each staff position read a third higher than treble (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clef, fetched).
The day CO2 first passed 400 ppm (May 9, 2013) is twice called a Tuesday. May 9, 2013 was a Thursday.

Monthly pay is computed as 4 weeks (26 h x $11.50 = $1,196). A month averages about 4.33 weeks, so it is about $1,296. HUD's 30% cost-burden test also uses gross income, but the story applies it to take-home pay.
The game is said to end one-nothing, a draw. A 1-0 score is a win, not a draw.

The story gives the strap in The Broken Column as green. The corset straps are pale grey/white metal-and-cloth; green appears only in the landscape (artincontext.org/the-broken-column-frida-kahlo, fetched).
